findings.external_fact: Neo-Hebbian three-factor learning and e-prop already provide delayed selective credit using local eligibility traces plus later modulatory/learning signals; direct biological eligibility-trace evidence also exists.
findings.implication: Delayed selective local credit is not a novelty discriminator; retain a minimal eligibility/return-address plus local-support null in P5.

findings.external_fact: A 2025 eLife study reports maintenance of a causal choice in a pending state across intervening decisions and later reinstatement at delayed feedback; the assessment notes limited ambiguity in the task.
findings.implication: P4 must exceed singleton pending-cause memory by preserving genuine simultaneous historical plurality until later independent evidence resolves it without privileged selection.

findings.external_fact: Bayesian latent-cause work demonstrates representation/inference over a full distribution of multiple possible hidden causes rather than only a MAP cause.
findings.implication: Plurality plus later evidence-based resolution is not conceptually novel; P5 should include an explicit latent-cause/belief-state null and account for its semantic/global-state privilege.

findings.external_fact: A peer-reviewed 2026 Frontiers paper learns synaptic and axonal delays online with three-factor rules in feedforward and recurrent LIF SNNs and reports material gains from learned delays.
findings.implication: Recent external literature independently strengthens the ordinary adaptive-delay interpretation of RV01 R01-17.

findings.external_fact: Recent TESS and Traces Propagation work demonstrates temporally/spatially local and forward-only SNN learning using local signals/eligibility mechanisms.
findings.implication: Locality, online operation and forward-only learning should be treated as constraints rather than novelty evidence; compare causal-resolution capability and privilege directly.
